summary: @servicetitan/standalone-root preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated 727KB payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs is obfuscator.io-style protected (renamed identifiers, per-function string dictionaries) and at npm install time downloads the Bun runtime v1.3.13 from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, then execFileSync's Bun against the sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB Bun-CJS bundle with a shuffled string/number array and hex-named identifiers, characteristic of obfuscator.io/obf-runtime protection. The manifest advertises a React/mobx frontend data-provider library for ServiceTitan MFEs, with peerDependencies on @servicetitan/* packages and a CHANGELOG that only references frontend PRs at github.com/servicetitan/standalone-fe — nothing in the advertised purpose requires an alternate JavaScript runtime or an opaque 727KB bundle, and neither setup.mjs nor math_init.js is referenced by dist/, src/, or the changelog. The alternate-runtime dropper pattern (fetch a non-Node runtime specifically to execute a heavily obfuscated sibling bundle) auto-fires on npm install and executes code whose behavior is not inspectable by Node-oriented tooling in the installer's environment.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
